title: Canonical exceptional tensor mate on an invertible input
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes, without absolute separatedness; all arrows are $k$-morphisms. Use $D^b_{ctf}$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], on small pro-etale sites, and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a separated finite-type arrow $u:T\to U$, write $F_u=Ru_!$, $G_u=Ru^!$ for compact supports and its transported constructible exceptional right adjoint [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $\varepsilon_u:F_uG_u\to1$ for its counit, and $\omega_u=G_u\Lambda_U$. Use the specified canonical tensor map $\theta_{u,P}:Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u\to G_uP$ and dualizing base-change map $\beta_{u,v}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; these maps are defined without assuming cohomological smoothness. All unit, symmetry and reassociation maps are the canonical derived ones.

Let $u:T\to U$ be separated of finite type and let $P\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ be tensor-invertible: there exists $P^{-1}\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ with $P\otimes^LP^{-1}\cong\Lambda_U$ and $P^{-1}\otimes^LP\cong\Lambda_U$. Then the specified canonical tensor map
$$\theta_{u,P}:Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u\xrightarrow{\sim}G_uP$$
is an isomorphism, natural in invertible inputs. In particular this asserts invertibility of the counit-defined mate of the projection formula, rather than just existence of an abstract isomorphism between its source and target. Neither cohomological smoothness of $u$ nor any dualizing base-change hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Write $F=Ru_!$, $G=Ru^!$, $H=Lu^*$, $\mathbf1=\Lambda_U$ and $\omega=G\mathbf1$. Work only on the full bounded constructible finite-Tor categories in the question. Their tensor closure is [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii). By [lem-pur-all-stage-ctf-pullback-unit], $Q=HP$ and $Q'=H(P^{-1})$ belong to the source category and $H\mathbf1\cong\Lambda_T$. Applying the tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] to the two given inverse isomorphisms gives $Q\otimes Q'\cong\Lambda_T$ and $Q'\otimes Q\cong\Lambda_T$. Hence right tensor by $Q$ on $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ has quasi-inverse right tensor by $Q'$, and right tensor by $P$ on the ambient category $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ has quasi-inverse right tensor by $P^{-1}$: the two composite comparisons are the associator followed by the given evaluation and the right unitor. The $U$-side is taken in the ambient category because $Ru_!$ is defined there [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and step 3 tests Hom sets out of $Ru_!B$; since $D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ is a full subcategory, its Hom sets are the ambient ones. All tensor symbols below mean derived tensor. The adjunction and $G\mathbf1\in D^b_{ctf}$ are exactly those specified in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], not an ambient pro-etale adjunction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection] to those two pairs of tensor functors. Thus $f\mapsto f\otimes1_Q$ and $a\mapsto a\otimes1_P$ are bijections on all relevant Hom sets. By [fix-prop-projection-formula], write $\pi_{B,P}:FB\otimes P\xrightarrow{\sim}F(B\otimes Q)$ for the specified projection isomorphism, natural in $B$ and $P$. Its hypotheses hold for every $B\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$, since $B$ is bounded constructible and $P$ has finite Tor amplitude. No smoothness or absolute separatedness is needed.

source.place: Final base-change sentence; agent expansion by tensor cancellation, Stacks Tag 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and the defining counit transpose

proof.text: Define $t:\omega\otimes Q\to GP$ by the adjunction transpose of $\lambda_P\circ(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1}\otimes1_P)\circ\pi_{\omega,P}^{-1}$, where $\lambda_P:\mathbf1\otimes P\cong P$. For each $B$ form the following bijection $\Psi_B$: start with $\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes Q,\omega\otimes Q)$, undo tensor by $Q$ to get $\operatorname{Hom}(B,\omega)$, transpose under $F\dashv G$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(FB,\mathbf1)$, tensor by $P$ and apply $\lambda_P$ to get $\operatorname{Hom}(FB\otimes P,P)$, precompose with $\pi_{B,P}^{-1}$, and transpose back to $\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes Q,GP)$. These are bijections by step 2 and the adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The definition [def-pur-co-smoothness] specifies precisely $\theta_{u,P}=t\circ\sigma_{Q,\omega}$; this uses its displayed transpose, not the assertion of cohomological smoothness.

source.place: Final base-change sentence; agent expansion by tensor cancellation, Stacks Tag 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and the defining counit transpose

proof.text:
Check the actual arrow underlying $\Psi_B$. Every input is uniquely $f\otimes1_Q$, with $f:B\to\omega$, by step 2. Its image under $\Psi_B$ has transpose
$$\lambda_P\circ((\varepsilon_{\mathbf1}\circ Ff)\otimes1_P)\circ\pi_{B,P}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of the projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives
$$(Ff\otimes1_P)\circ\pi_{B,P}^{-1}=\pi_{\omega,P}^{-1}\circ F(f\otimes1_Q).$$
Consequently that transpose is
$$\lambda_P\circ(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1}\otimes1_P)\circ\pi_{\omega,P}^{-1}\circ F(f\otimes1_Q),$$
which is the transpose of $t\circ(f\otimes1_Q)$ by the defining equation of $t$ and naturality of the adjunction. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $\Psi_B(h)=t\circ h$ for every $h$. Thus postcomposition by this specified $t$ is bijective on tests $B\otimes Q$.

source.place: Final base-change sentence; agent expansion by tensor cancellation, Stacks Tag 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and the defining counit transpose

proof.text: Every source object $A$ is isomorphic to $B\otimes Q$ with $B=A\otimes Q'$: use $\alpha_{A,Q',Q}$, the evaluation $Q'\otimes Q\cong\Lambda_T$ and the right unitor. Precomposition with this isomorphism identifies the Hom tests, so step 4 makes postcomposition by $t$ bijective for every $A$. For $A=GP$ choose $s:GP\to\omega\otimes Q$ with $t\circ s=1$. For $A=\omega\otimes Q$, injectivity and $t\circ(s\circ t)=t=t\circ1$ imply $s\circ t=1$. Hence $t$ is an isomorphism, and so is $\theta_{u,P}=t\circ\sigma_{Q,\omega}$. This is the elementary two-test Yoneda argument, written out rather than invoked as an uncited theorem.

source.place: Final base-change sentence; agent expansion by tensor cancellation, Stacks Tag 0FFM (categories-lemma-invertible) and the defining counit transpose

proof.text:
For a morphism $a:P\to\widetilde P$ of invertible inputs, let $\widetilde Q=H\widetilde P$ and $\widetilde t$ be the same transpose construction. Projection naturality in the second argument [fix-prop-projection-formula] says
$$(F\omega\otimes a)\circ\pi_{\omega,P}^{-1}=\pi_{\omega,\widetilde P}^{-1}\circ F(1_\omega\otimes Ha).$$
After composing with the counit and unitors, both sides transpose to
$$G(a)\circ t=\widetilde t\circ(1_\omega\otimes Ha).$$
Here the unitor equation is $a\circ\lambda_P=\lambda_{\widetilde P}\circ(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes a)$, and transposition is natural by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Finally naturality of symmetry gives $G(a)\circ\theta_{u,P}=\theta_{u,\widetilde P}\circ(Ha\otimes1_\omega)$, proving the asserted naturality of the canonical isomorphisms.
